name: jcal
desc: UNIX-cal-like tool to display Jalali calendar
why: A cal clone for the Jalali calendar is a small cultural door, though it is mostly a single-purpose utility.

brief.what_it_is: jcal is a Jalali (Persian/Solar Hijri) calendar package on Savannah. Its homepage describes it as "A library and a set of terminal tools for Jalali Calendar." The Homebrew metadata gives the short description "UNIX-cal-like tool to display Jalali calendar" and two executables, jcal and jdate. I could not read a README, so I cannot confirm the exact inputs and outputs or flags. The likely pattern is a cal-style monthly grid printed to the terminal, plus a date-conversion tool, but that is inferred from the names and not verified.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motivation. The short description suggests it exists to bring a familiar UNIX cal-style display to the Jalali calendar.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, I saw no build or configuration steps. The Savannah download area offers source tarballs (jcal-0.6.0.tar.gz and jcal-latest.tar.gz, both 434 KiB, dated 2026-May-21) with GPG signatures, so a source build is possible. I did not open the tarball and cannot say what it needs to build.
brief.standout: It is a small, single-purpose tool for a calendar most UNIX users have never used, packaged as a library plus terminal commands. The Savannah page is an unusually plain, GNU-hosted home for a niche utility.
brief.status: Maintained, with mixed evidence. The latest release is 0.6.0, dated 2026-May-21 on the Savannah download index, and the project is marked Development Status 5 - Production/Stable. Earlier releases date from 2011 (0.2.0 through 0.4.1), so there was a long gap before 0.6.0. The Savannah page shows no news items and zero open bugs out of one total. I did not check a commit log.
brief.caveats: I could not read a README. The homepage is only the Savannah project summary page, and the Docs link was not followed, so this brief lacks the author's own usage examples and commands. The project is not part of the GNU Project. Licence is GNU GPL v3 or later. Platform support is unknown.
